facts.text: Health ministers meet in Winnipeg Oct. 15-16, hosted by Manitoba's Uzoma Asagwara
Federal Health Minister Marjorie Michel announced on social media a one-year, $1.2-billion extension of mental health, addictions and home care funding
Provincial and territorial ministers said Oct. 1 they were united in calling on Ottawa to be 'a full and committed funding partner'
P/T ministers warned of 'profound and negative' effects on patients and health-care jobs if agreements lapse
Expiring funds: $4.8B over four years for home/community care and mental health; $3B for long-term care safety; $1.7B for PSW wages
The 2023 federal pledge was $200 billion in health funding over 10 years
Canada Health Transfer grows 5 per cent a year until 2028, then a minimum 3 per cent
Asagwara: 'I feel Minister Michel has been listening'
N.L. Health Minister Joedy Wall said Humberwood and Corner Brook projects won't be affected if funding lapses
CMA and nurses' unions jointly backed provinces' call for predictable CHT funding and urged passage of Bills S-5 and C-34
Finance Minister Champagne committed to continuing talks with provinces on immediate health funding pressures
Health Canada renewed the Working Together agreement with N.W.T.: $51.2 million over seven years, first of a series
Provinces ask Ottawa to renew $1.2B a year, commit to at least 5 per cent CHT growth after 2028, and be a full funding partner
CMAJ commentary says the spring economic update already set the CHT increase to fall from 5 to 3 per cent in April 2028
Ontario Health Minister Sylvia Jones is cited by an aggregator piece as flagging federal-provincial tension over CHT
Provinces want the 5 per cent CHT floor to hold past 2028
News conferences: P/T Thursday 4 p.m. CT; FPT Friday 3 p.m. CT
No on-record Ontario response to the extension found

missed.text: Asagwara called the funding expiry a 'looming fiscal cliff' with 'devastating consequences'
CFNU's Linda Silas said health care must be balanced against defence and other spending: 'There has to be a just balance'
The Canadian Press corrected its story; an earlier version used an incorrect pronoun for Asagwara
No Ontario government statement or on-record comment from Jones or Premier Ford on the extension was found
